$comment: Parity ledger between pi-dsh and DeepSeek Harness. pi-dsh is a semantic reimplementation, so drift is tracked explicitly: run `npm run check:drift -- [path-to-deepseek-harness]` to list upstream commits since the pin that touch mapped packages, review them, then bump dsh.commit (the script's --update-pin does this after your review). Status values: ported | partial | not-ported | not-applicable.

gaps: Plan approval needs an interactive UI because there is no ask_user_question tool; without one plan mode stays on and /plan off is the only exit.
Plan mode takes effect at once, where DSH holds a user selection until the next accepted pre-step.
areas.notes: exit_plan_mode fails closed without a UI: plan mode stays on and the plan goes to the user as the reply.

Rounds are admitted at Pi's agent_before_settle boundary (continue + custom_message) instead of DSH's Agent.followup(); abort pauses an admitted round and disarms otherwise, /goal pause aborts the live turn, error outcomes disarm, and a round that never reaches its first turn blocks the goal (queue-failed). Each round prompt carries its goalId, revision and round; at the next turn start it must still own the goal (same id and revision, active and armed, next round number, no message from the user waiting) or it is withdrawn: not counted, and replaced by a stand-down notice in every later request. Not ported: wrap-up context after complete/blocked.
gaps: No wrap-up instruction after complete or blocked; the turn simply continues.

areas.notes: DSH's agent inbox is a durable projection with next-turn and next-step lanes. pi-dsh keeps its own notices (job/subagent/agent-message/goal/timeout) in a session-entry outbox, drained at Pi's turn_end and agent_before_settle boundaries with coalescing, key-based replacement, and a /inbox view. Not ported: item-level edit and lane transfer, and a durable lane for the user's own steer/follow-up messages, which Pi keeps in memory.
gaps: No item-level edit or lane transfer.
No durable lane for the user's own steer and follow-up messages, which Pi keeps in memory.

areas.notes: A pi-dsh addition. DSH keeps durable user instructions in AGENTS.md (agent-instructions) and in its LLM-written checkpoint ('Critical Context'). pi-vcc compacts algorithmically and can drop a rule list, so rules_write stores them as session entries and re-injects them in the control section after every compaction.
gaps: Not a port: DSH keeps durable instructions in AGENTS.md and its LLM-written checkpoint, while rules_write stores a rules list as session entries.

areas.notes: Repeat reminders 3/5/8; read-before-edit + stale-version; tool deadlines: timeout input caps on all tools, fused AbortSignal deadlines for nested executeTool calls, configurable top-level watchdog (toolTimeoutMs) that aborts and stamps TOOL_TIMEOUT. DSH timeout-policy is likewise cooperative (it cannot hard-stop a tool that ignores exec.signal); the residual Pi gap is that a model-issued foreign call's signal cannot be swapped per-call, so top-level enforcement aborts the turn, not just the call.
gaps: A top-level tool deadline aborts the turn, not only the call, because Pi cannot swap the signal of a model-issued call.

areas.notes: Pruning mirrors DSH's persistent, replay-safe tool-result pruner: replacements are stored as Pi context_edit entries at turn_end instead of request-time rewrites. Unlike DSH (which prunes at compaction, every over-budget result), pi-dsh triggers on context-window pressure and leaves the newest six tool results whole; head/tail budgets are 8000 chars per result rather than DSH's 4096+1024.
gaps: Pruning triggers on context pressure and keeps the newest six results whole; DSH prunes every over-budget result at compaction.
Head and tail budget is 8000 characters per result, not 4096 and 1024.

areas.notes: Sandbox: bubblewrap profile + escalation approval + cached functional probe + sandboxRunnerCommand override (DSH runnerCommand). DSH Linux fallback Landlock runner is not ported; bubblewrap only, fails closed. A cancelled shell job gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after jobKillGraceMs (default 3000), and the settled job records the kill reason.
gaps: No Landlock fallback runner; bubblewrap only.
A killed job records the caller's reason, not DSH's signal-plus-cause detail.

areas.notes: Backends: node-pty, util-linux script, and tmux for durable=true. Durable tmux terminals survive a pi exit and reattach on restore; all terminals persist a transcript, and dead non-durable terminals restore as exited stubs (shell state cannot be resurrected). pwsh tools register only when a binary exists.
gaps: A non-durable terminal's shell state cannot survive a restart; it restores as an exited stub.

areas.notes: Tree-wide capacity (8), maxSubagentDepth (default 1) with child-visible delegation tools below the cap, adjacent messaging both directions with messageIds, per-child model/thinking/preset selection, timeouts, progress/activity via agent_status, descriptor-persisted catalog (result replay + cold resume after restart), and the agent-team board (CAS revisions, blockedBy readiness, writeScope overlap warnings, wait-for-change) visible to teammates as scoped tools. Deltas: presets are pi-dsh config objects, not DSH preset-registry compositions; interrupt waits for settle instead of returning on acceptance; child bash honors the standing sandboxMode through a confined foreground bash (no owned background jobs in children); team state is one board per root session persisted as session entries. pi-dsh addition with no DSH counterpart: isolation="worktree" (DSH agent-team shares one workspace and offers only advisory writeScopes overlap warnings and no Git controls). subagentModels is an allowlist of provider/modelId routes applied to every explicit selection, a preset's or workflow agent's model included, and inheriting the parent's model is never gated (dsh ModelSelectionPolicy gates only the model-facing fields).
gaps: External providers are partial (next area).
Presets are config objects, not preset-registry compositions.
Interrupt waits for the child to settle instead of returning on acceptance.
Children have a confined foreground bash only, with no owned background jobs.
Team state is one board per root session.

areas.notes: Opt-in through externalSubagents in pi-dsh.json: each entry (claude-code, codex, or acp with a command) adds a subagent_<name> tool. Like DSH, a run is one unattended session of the product in the workspace: the task in, the final answer or a fixed-shape failure diagnostic out, ambient credentials scrubbed from its environment, no follow-up input, reasoning and stderr kept out of the parent session. It goes through the installed CLI (claude -p with stream-json, codex exec --json) or an ACP server over stdio, not DSH's pinned SDK and app-server runtimes. Choosing a provider never widens access: Codex takes the standing sandboxMode as its own --sandbox, Claude Code is limited to an allowlist of file tools, with no MCP servers or skills, under a restrictive mode (acceptEdits by default under workspace-write), a permission setting wider than the sandbox is refused, and an ACP agent runs under bubblewrap with writablePaths for its own state. Also list_subagent_models does not cover these products.
gaps: Claude Code and ACP were run against the real products on a few tasks only (GLM via a Z.ai plan; opencode as the ACP agent); Codex only against its real binary with a local stand-in model server.
Codex runs through codex exec, not the app-server protocol, and its approval modes map onto one permission setting.
ACP declares no fs or terminal client capabilities and has no authenticate step; the agent must be logged in beforehand.
No Plugins-page bundle, and an external run never resumes after a restart.

areas.notes: Plus a mossbed backend with no DSH equivalent. Resource limits mirror ptc-runtime-node: ptcMaxOutputBytes (64 MiB), ptcMaxPendingCalls (128), ptcMaxMessageBytes (128 MiB). The Python backend runs under the same bubblewrap profile as Node, and both keep a stderr tail for crash diagnostics. A program stopped by a timeout, an abort or a limit gets SIGTERM and then SIGKILL after ptcGraceMs (3000), and the logs it had already written come back with the failure.
gaps: The mossbed backend is killed at once on timeout or abort, with no SIGTERM grace or streamed output.
The Python backend keeps no state between calls.
No Landlock fallback runner; bubblewrap only.
No per-agent provider override, and agent() takes no isolation option.
No persisted run record.
areas.notes: parallel() and pipeline() follow the dsh guest: pipeline chains stages per item with no cross-stage barrier, a bad argument or tripped cap (workflowMaxAgents, workflowMaxItemsPerCall) ends the script while a failed child nulls only its item, and the script runs under the standing sandbox mode. A script that dies leaves no child running. The first synchronous stretch of a script, up to its first await, runs under workflowSyncTimeoutMs (5000), as in DSH; a loop after an await is ended only by an abort.

DSH ships web/desktop React panels. A Pi extension can draw footer status + string-array widgets, so pi-dsh renders goal/todos/jobs/agents-terminals-team widgets and a /dsh dashboard instead (src/ui.ts). No clickable panels, no graphs.
gaps: No clickable panels and no graphs.

areas.notes: dsh-sandbox-ssh confines processes launched by DSH's SSH subprocess/filesystem providers through a remote helper. pi-dsh has no SSH transport to confine; porting the sandbox without an SSH execution feature would be dead code. Local bubblewrap is the applicable boundary.
Out of scope by maintainer decision: pi-dsh is Linux-tested.
